prompt: Put the author's protocol steps in order.

options.why: Step 1: everything else needs the relaxed structure.

options.text: SCF in the same folder with ISTART = 1 and LORBIT = 11
options.why: Step 2: writes CHGCAR and the DOS.

options.text: Band structure along KPATH.in from VASPKIT 303
options.why: Step 3: needs the converged density.

options.text: Elastic constants with IBRION = 6 and ENCUT = 620
options.why: Step 4: needs the relaxed structure.

options.text: Optics with LOPTICS and three times the default NBANDS
options.why: Step 5: needs more empty bands.

prompt: Why does the protocol use ENCUT = 1.3 x ENMAX for the relaxation?

options.text: So that the stress converges; a too-small basis gives a Pulay stress that distorts the cell
options.why: Stress converges more slowly with ENCUT than the energy.
Tempting, but a higher cutoff makes it slower.
Tempting, but VASP accepts any ENCUT.

hints: The cell changes during the relaxation.

prompt: Why does the elastic step comment out NCORE?

options.text: IBRION = 6 runs without band parallelization, and NCORE in the INCAR can stop the run
options.why: As recorded with protocol step 4.
Tempting, but parallel settings never change converged physics.

options.text: NCORE is only for spin-polarised runs
options.why: Tempting, but NCORE applies to all runs.

hints: It is about how VASP splits the work.
The protocol note gives the reason.

prompt: The SCF OUTCAR reports NBANDS = 52. Following step 5, what is three times that, before rounding up for the core count?
Why must the band-structure eigenvalues not come from a self-consistent run on the KPATH.in line path?

options.text: A line path does not sample the zone evenly, so the self-consistent density would be wrong
options.why: Use route A (KPOINTS_OPT) or route B (ICHARG = 11).

options.text: KPATH.in has the wrong file format
options.why: Tempting, but it is a valid line-mode KPOINTS.
Tempting, but 211 reads band runs.

hints: The VASP wiki says line mode is not suitable for SCF.

prompt: The relaxation and SCF share a folder. What should you do before starting the SCF?

options.text: Copy CONTCAR to POSCAR and back up the relaxation OUTCAR and CONTCAR
options.why: The SCF overwrites them.
Tempting for a clean start, but ISTART = 1 needs it.

options.text: Change ENCUT to the POTCAR default
options.why: Tempting, but the SCF keeps the converged settings.

hints: Which files will the SCF overwrite?

prompt: What does a line starting with #SBATCH do?

options.text: It gives a request to the SLURM scheduler, such as the number of nodes
options.why: The shell sees a comment; sbatch reads the directive.

options.text: It is a comment with no effect
options.why: Tempting because of the #, but sbatch reads these lines.
Tempting, but VASP is started by srun or mpirun.

hints: PBS uses #PBS for the same purpose.

prompt: Which executable do you use for a spin-orbit coupling run?

options.why: Non-collinear magnetism and spin-orbit coupling need the ncl build.
Tempting because it is fast, but it is for Gamma-point-only runs.
Tempting as the default, but it is collinear only.

hints: Spin-orbit couples spin direction to the lattice.

prompt: A job hit its wall-time limit during a relaxation. What should you check first?

options.text: That CONTCAR is complete before copying it to POSCAR
options.why: A job killed while writing can leave CONTCAR empty or truncated.
Tempting, but VASP never writes POTCAR.
Tempting, but VASP does not change your INCAR.

hints: Which file is rewritten after every ionic step?

prompt: How do you submit job.sh on a PBS cluster?

options.why: PBS uses qsub; SLURM uses sbatch.
Tempting, but that is SLURM.
Tempting, but that runs it on the login node without the scheduler.

prompt: You change NCORE from 4 to 8 and the converged energy changes by 20 meV. What does this tell you?

options.text: Something else is wrong, such as an unconverged run; parallel settings do not change converged results
options.why: NCORE changes speed and memory, not physics.
Tempting, but parallel tags are not accuracy settings.

options.text: This is the normal size of the effect
options.why: Tempting, but the energies must agree to numerical precision.

prompt: What does KPAR do?

options.text: Splits the k-points into groups that are computed side by side
options.why: Each group of ranks handles a share of the k-points.
Tempting from the name, but the mesh is set by KPOINTS.

options.text: Sets the number of cores per band
options.why: Tempting, but that is NCORE.

hints: K for k-points, PAR for parallel.
It does not change the mesh.

prompt: A job has 64 MPI ranks with KPAR = 4 and NCORE = 4. How many band groups are there in each k-point group?
Why should KPAR not exceed the number of irreducible k-points?

options.text: Some k-point groups would have nothing to compute
options.why: Those cores sit idle.
Tempting, but VASP never changes your mesh for parallelism.
Tempting, but parallel settings do not change the result.

hints: More groups than points means idle groups.

prompt: Which ISTART does the protocol use for the SCF after the relaxation?

options.text: 1, read WAVECAR and keep ENCUT constant
options.why: The relaxation left a WAVECAR in the same folder.
Tempting for safety, but it throws away nearly converged wavefunctions.
Tempting, but it is used rarely, for example along a strained series.

prompt: What does ICHARG = 11 do?

options.text: Reads CHGCAR and keeps it fixed, for band structures and dense-mesh DOS
options.why: Non-self-consistent: only the eigenvalues are computed.
Tempting, but that is ICHARG = 1.
Tempting, but that is ICHARG = 2.

prompt: Which must be identical between the SCF and an ICHARG = 11 run that reads its CHGCAR? Select all that apply.

options.why: Part of the rule in the Workflow Handbook.
The stored magnetization must match.
The density belongs to one structure.
Tempting, but changing the k-points is the point of the band run.

hints: The run inherits its physics from CHGCAR.
What changes in a band run?

prompt: An SCF stalled after 200 steps. How can you continue from its last density?

options.text: ICHARG = 1 with the CHGCAR from that run
options.why: It reads the density and continues self-consistently.
Tempting, but that keeps the density fixed and never converges it.
Tempting, but that starts again from atoms.

hints: You want to continue, not freeze.

prompt: Why must LMAXMIX be kept when reading a CHGCAR of a d or f element compound?

options.text: CHGCAR stores the PAW one-centre occupancies only up to LMAXMIX
options.why: Set 4 for d, 6 for f elements, in both runs.

options.text: LMAXMIX sets the number of k-points
options.why: Tempting, but it is about angular momentum in the mixer and CHGCAR.
Tempting, but the Workflow Handbook lists it in the rule.

hints: What is stored besides the grid?

prompt: In OSZICAR, an ionic step used 60 electronic steps with NELM = 60. What does this mean?

options.text: That step did not converge electronically; its forces are unreliable
options.why: VASP continues anyway; fix the mixing.

options.text: It converged exactly at the limit
options.why: Tempting, but reaching NELM means the loop was stopped, not converged.
Tempting, but a typical step needs far fewer.

hints: VASP does not stop on its own.

prompt: What is E0 on an OSZICAR ionic line?

options.text: The energy extrapolated to zero smearing
options.why: For Gaussian smearing quote E0 when comparing energies.

options.text: The energy of the first electronic step
options.why: Tempting because of the 0, but it is sigma to 0.
Tempting, but VASP does not compute vibrations here.

prompt: Which OUTCAR line confirms that a relaxation met EDIFFG?

options.why: Without it the run stopped at NSW or was killed.
Tempting, but that only says the run ended.
Tempting, but that is the Fermi energy.

prompt: OUTCAR: energy without entropy = -45.120 eV, TOTEN = -45.128 eV, 8 atoms. What is T*S per atom in meV?
hints: Divide by the number of atoms and convert to meV.

prompt: With EDIFFG = -0.01 the largest force in the last TOTAL-FORCE table is 0.03 eV per angstrom. What do you conclude?

options.text: The structure is not relaxed to the criterion
options.why: Every force must be below 0.01.
Tempting, but 0.03 is three times the limit.
Tempting, but there is no reason to doubt it.

prompt: Which are signs of trouble in a relaxation? Select all that apply.

options.why: The run stopped before meeting EDIFFG.

options.text: Ionic steps that used NELM electronic steps
options.why: Those steps did not converge.
SIGMA is too large (Heuristic: about 1 meV).

options.text: dE falling by several orders of magnitude within each ionic step
options.why: Tempting to worry about, but that is healthy convergence.

prompt: Which VASPKIT task writes KPATH.in for a band structure?

options.why: Protocol step 3: vaspkit 3, then 303.
Tempting because it writes KPOINTS, but 102 is the uniform SCF mesh.
Tempting, but 211 reads the band result.

prompt: What does the 101 task code SRMG produce?

options.why: SR is standard relaxation, MG adds magnetism.

options.text: A static run with spin-orbit coupling
options.why: Tempting, but that would be ST and SO.
Tempting, but 101 writes INCAR templates.

prompt: You run 101 in a folder where you hand-edited INCAR. With default settings, what happens?

options.why: Set BACK-UP-OLD or BACK-UP-NEW to protect it.
Tempting, but the default mode overwrites.
Tempting, but it runs and overwrites.

prompt: A menu number from a tutorial does nothing in your VASPKIT. Why?

options.text: Menus change between releases; check the menu of your installed version
options.why: The codes here are from VASPKIT 1.5.
Tempting, but the menus are VASPKIT's, not VASP's.
Tempting, but that only applies to tasks that build POTCAR.

hints: The caveat is on the page.
Which version is the map from?

prompt: Which VASPKIT task should you run before every submission?

options.why: It fixes INCAR and POSCAR format and checks POTCAR against POSCAR.
Tempting, but that builds a structure; it does not check.
Tempting, but that is analysis after a run.
